questions.text: The area of the large piston of a hydraulic press is 5 dm² and that of the small piston is 20 cm². If the small piston of the press is pushed with a force of 500 N, what force is produced on the large piston (kN)?
If a force of 100 N acts on the small piston of a hydraulic press with an area of 10 cm², what force is produced on the large piston with an area of 1 m² (N)?
The area of the large piston of a hydraulic press is 375 cm². What must the area of the small piston be (cm²) in order to lift a load weighing 12 kN by acting on it with a force of 160 N?
The area of the small piston of a hydraulic jack is 2.4 cm², and the force acting on it is 1000 N. If the area of the large piston is 2880 cm², what mass of load (in tonnes) can this jack lift?
What load (kg) must be placed on the large piston in the system shown in the figure so that it does not move? S2 = 4.5S1 (the load on the small piston is 5 kg).

The area of the small piston of a hydraulic press is 8 cm² and that of the large piston is 800 cm². When a force of 600 N is applied to the small piston, a force of 54 kN is obtained from the large piston. By how many times can this press increase the force without friction and with friction?
The area of the small piston of a hydraulic press is 4 cm² and that of the large one is 500 cm². If the small piston is pushed down at 25 cm/s, at what speed does the large piston rise (cm/s)?
The small piston of a hydraulic press moved down 15 cm under a force of 60 N. If the large piston rose 5 cm in the process, what force (in newtons) acted on the large piston?

The small piston of a hydraulic press is acted upon through a lever whose arms are in the ratio 1:5. If the areas of the pistons of the hydraulic press differ by a factor of 4, what total gain in force does this mechanism provide?
